description: Six-panel composite figure mixing SEM and TEM micrographs with selected-area electron diffraction, all addressing where kappa-carbide precipitates in Fe-Mn-Al-C steel. (a) SEM, 20 µm scale bar: a grain-boundary network decorated by bright particles labelled "κ" and "α" (with arrows). (b) TEM, 0.5 µm scale bar: γ austenite matrix with a κ-carbide band along a boundary; the inset SAED (transmitted spot "T") carries spots labelled 100 and 0ī1. (c) SEM, 4 µm scale bar: lamellar structure of alternating α and γ plates with thin κ films/lamellae along interfaces. (d) TEM, 1 µm scale bar: intragranular γ, κ plates and γ_twin twins, with an inset SAED labelled 0ī1 and ī10. (e) TEM, 0.5 µm scale bar: κ, α and γ coexisting, κ decorating boundaries while also lying within grains. (f) standalone SAED, 5 1/nm scale bar, whose spots form a hexagonal ring labelled 200, 101, 111, 110 around the transmitted spot T. Together the panels argue that κ-carbide adopts intergranular (a, b), intragranular (c, d) and simultaneous intergranular-plus-intragranular (e, f) distributions within the austenite matrix. No composition or property values are printed; only scale bars and phase/spot labels are shown.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph, 20 µm scale bar: grain boundaries decorated by bright precipitates labelled κ, with arrows marking particles labelled α; a small arrow marker sits at the top-left corner.
TEM bright-field micrograph, 0.5 µm scale bar: γ matrix (top) against a κ-carbide band at a grain boundary; inset SAED pattern with transmitted spot T and spots labelled 100 and 0ī1.
SEM micrograph, 4 µm scale bar: lamellar/rod-like two-phase structure with light plates labelled α and γ, and κ films/lamellae along interfaces and boundaries.
TEM bright-field micrograph, 1 µm scale bar: γ matrix, κ lamellae and γ_twin twins; inset SAED pattern with spots labelled 0ī1 and ī10.
TEM micrograph, 0.5 µm scale bar: mixed structure labelled κ, α and γ, showing κ both along a grain boundary and within the grain interior.
Standalone SAED pattern, 5 1/nm scale bar: diffraction spots arranged in a hexagonal ring around the transmitted spot T, with spots labelled 200, 101, 111 and 110.

observations.observation: The figure is a six-panel composite: (a) and (c) are SEM micrographs, (b), (d) and (e) are TEM bright-field micrographs (b and d with SAED insets), and (f) is a standalone SAED pattern.
Panel (a) has a 20 µm scale bar and shows a grain-boundary network decorated by bright particles labelled κ, with arrows pointing to particles labelled α.
Panel (b) has a 0.5 µm scale bar and its inset SAED pattern shows a transmitted spot marked T together with spots labelled 100 and 0ī1.
Panel (c) has a 4 µm scale bar and shows alternating α and γ plates with κ films/lamellae along the interfaces.
Panel (d) has a 1 µm scale bar and is labelled with γ, κ and γ_twin; its inset SAED pattern shows spots labelled 0ī1 and ī10.
Panel (e) has a 0.5 µm scale bar and shows κ, α and γ labelled together, with κ appearing both at a boundary and within the grain.
Panel (f) has a 5 1/nm scale bar and shows a hexagonal ring of diffraction spots around the transmitted spot T, with spots labelled 200, 101, 111 and 110.
The caption states that (a, b) show κ*-carbide precipitated along grain boundary.
The caption states that (c, d) show κ-carbide precipitated within grain.
The caption states that (e, f) show κ-carbide precipitated simultaneously along grain boundary and within grain.
The citing text states that κ-carbide can be divided into intragranular κ0-carbides and intergranular κ*-carbides, as shown in Fig. 2.
The citing text states that after cold rolling the severe plastic deformation elongates numerous grains into lath-like morphology along the rolling direction.
